nodes.label: Unattended Run Discipline
nodes.rationale: Because nobody can answer questions, ambiguities go to QUESTIONS.md with the most conservative interpretation implemented and marked `# TODO(QUESTIONS.md): <ref>`; invariants are never relaxed to make something work; scope is never expanded; no system software installs, history rewrites, or force-pushes.

nodes.label: Checkpoint Protocol
nodes.rationale: State the ID and done-when criterion, implement, test, run pytest, commit on pass or commit as '(tests failing)' with a diagnosis on failure and move on. Never stall, never delete or weaken a test to make it pass, never leave uncommitted work at a checkpoint boundary.

nodes.label: A0 Comes First — Contract Before Apps
nodes.rationale: Schemas are defined once with a schema_version and imported by both sides because divergence surfaces as a crash on real data months from now. Round-trip tests (acquisition writes a synthetic session, analysis reads it into a manifest) are the contract's proof and exist from A0 onward.

nodes.label: Anticipated Drift Paths
nodes.rationale: Named in advance as invariant violations: unbounded frame queue, PySpin before the mock path, QC dropping rows instead of marking included=False, undistorting video instead of coordinates, hardcoded thresholds, welding the stop condition into the Qt handler, GUI stylesheets, silently bridging long interpolation gaps.

nodes.label: Zero-Dependency Testing Requirement
nodes.rationale: No test may require DLC, PySpin, CUDA or a network mount — that is what makes an unattended run verifiable. The bounded-queue drop behaviour, the trial state machine guards, and the kinematics ground-truth recovery are the three places tests earn their keep.
